title: Attention Basin: Why Contextual Position Matters in Large Language Models

title: Positional Encoding via Token-Aware Phase Attention
relation_to_ours: formal RoPE distance decay: newest tokens dominate; far stale values attenuated

title: Base of RoPE Bounds Context Length
relation_to_ours: RoPE base sets how fast recency decay bites; basis for per-family reporting (D4)

title: Evaluating Memory Condensation Strategies for Coding Agents in Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
relation_to_ours: Independent OpenHands-condenser study: 8 condensers, accuracy flat, LLM summaries +24-94% tokens, masking -8.6%; no cache accounting. L3 analog.

title: The OpenHands Software Agent SDK: A Composable and Extensible Foundation for Production Agents
relation_to_ours: Documents the production condenser (up to 2x per-turn API cost claim, vendor-reported); the shipped compaction we contrast L1 against.

title: Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents -- A Source-Code Study of Eleven Systems
relation_to_ours: Source-code anatomy of 11 harnesses incl. context management; evidence that append-only plus compaction is the de facto layout (our L1).

title: AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management
relation_to_ours: Per-step folding over multi-scale state summary; L3 family; its consolidated state block is a trained cousin of L4 recitation (D3).

title: FoldAct: Efficient and Stable Context Folding for Long-Horizon Search Agents
relation_to_ours: Shows summaries make the observation distribution policy-dependent and unstable; mechanistic reason rewritten contexts (L2/L3) differ from L1 at equal information.

title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
relation_to_ours: Optimised compression guidelines, 26-54% peak-token cut, >95% accuracy kept, small models gain up to 46%; no caching. Strong trained-compression baseline; mirror of D4.

title: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
relation_to_ours: Periodic external summariser plus RL; +4.5%/+8.2% on BrowseComp; L3b-style summary arm with no cost accounting.

title: MemAgent: Reshaping Long-Context LLM with Multi-Conv RL-based Memory Agent
relation_to_ours: Overwrite-memory agent; the extreme of L3 (nothing stale retained); reference point for the stale-value mechanism (D1).

title: Toward Reliable Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents: An Empirical Study of Execution Instability
relation_to_ours: Compression weakens recency, raises blocked/repeated actions and run instability (AppWorld); motivates our repeat-call noise floor and stale-trap annotation; informs D3 failure explanation.

title: StateComp: Learning When to Compress History in Long Horizon Agents
relation_to_ours: Learns when a past interaction is safe to replace (KEEP/READY); our L3 placeholder rule is an oracle version of READY; closest formalisation of 'superseded'.

title: InfiAgent: An Infinite-Horizon Framework for General-Purpose Autonomous Agents
relation_to_ours: Rebuilds context from a file state snapshot plus recent window each step (cache-hostile); contrast for L4 which restates state without rewriting history.

title: A Self-Evolving Framework for Efficient Terminal Agents via Observational Context Compression
relation_to_ours: Training-free observation compression (TACO); observation-level L3 with token cost only, no caching.

title: What to Keep, What to Forget: A Rate--Distortion View of Memory Compaction in LLMs and Agents
relation_to_ours: Unifying taxonomy; states that repeated compaction as agents perform it is almost never measured, which is where L3 vs L1 sits.

title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale
relation_to_ours: Production KV-cache hit ~90% within turn, ~55% at turn boundaries, drastic invalidation after compaction/model switch; external anchor for L1 hit fraction and for L3 as the cache-breaking event (D5).

title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving
relation_to_ours: ~4,300 Claude Code/Codex sessions; high-but-imperfect prefix hits, better on tool-result continuations than after pauses; supports 100:1 regime and our TTL discipline.

title: Agentic AI Workload Characteristics
relation_to_ours: With caching most input tokens are reused and serving becomes decode-dominated; serving-side reason layout discipline is enforced; no accuracy.

title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
relation_to_ours: AgentSysBench; names tool schemas/observations as context overhead; tool-result caching removes 35.2% redundant searches; background only.

title: PrefixBench-H100: Characterizing Prefix Reuse and Time-to-First-Token in H100 LLM Serving
relation_to_ours: Prefix-reuse benchmark; hit statistics and TTFT regimes; minor, supports optional vLLM arm metrics.

title: Recency/Frequency Adaptive KV Caching for Large Language Model Serving
relation_to_ours: Adaptive eviction raises hit rate up to 10.8%; shows observed hit rate is serving-dependent, so we log observed not nominal hits.

title: Generative Caching for Structurally Similar Prompts and Responses
relation_to_ours: Response-level generative cache (~83% hit); tangential, cited to distinguish prefix caching from response caching.

title: Token Economics for LLM Agents: A Dual-View Study from Computing and Economics
relation_to_ours: Survey of token cost as economic primitive; related-work framing for USD per correct task; no measurements.

title: A Comprehensive Empirical Evaluation of Agent Frameworks on Code-centric Software Engineering Tasks
relation_to_ours: Seven frameworks; monetary cost and token overhead reported; one of few framework comparisons that mentions input caching; no layout control.

title: The Scaffold Effect in Coding Agents: Harness Choice as a Hidden Variable in Coding-Agent Evaluation
relation_to_ours: Up to 40x tokens per solved task across harnesses with 0-8 pp pass-rate change; establishes tokens-per-solved-task reporting; no caching.

title: The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI
relation_to_ours: Orchestration swap: $0.21 to $0.12 per task at parity quality; USD per task from list prices with no cache split, the term that drives D5.

title: The Scaffolding Matters More Than the Interface: A Controlled Comparison of MCP and CLI Tool Use Across Seven Agent Scaffoldings, Five Language Models, and One Software Task
relation_to_ours: Scaffolding dominates USD cost (5-28x; 139x for a 27B model); MCP schema injection is a large cost term; justifies fixed shared tool block across L1-L4.

title: AgentSlimming: Towards Efficient and Cost-Aware Multi-Agent Systems
relation_to_ours: Prunes redundant agents, up to 78.9% token cost cut; multi-agent token-waste line; orthogonal to layout.

title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
relation_to_ours: Cost-controlled harness, 21,730 rollouts, ~$40k; reporting standard (accuracy vs USD) we adopt; no layout variation, no cache-read split.

title: Cost-of-Pass: An Economic Framework for Evaluating Language Models
relation_to_ours: Defines cost-of-pass = expected USD per correct solution; names our metric; list prices without caching, which our billed usage.cost corrects.

title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks with Dense Reward-Based Grading
relation_to_ours: Pass rate vs estimated USD per task (June-2026 list prices); more spend does not buy long-horizon success; estimated not billed cost.

title: Inference-Time Distillation: Cost-Efficient Agents Without Fine-Tuning or Manual Prompt Engineering
relation_to_ours: Shifts cost-accuracy Pareto frontier for agents via ICL and cascades; frontier over methods, ours is over layouts.

title: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
relation_to_ours: Token-matched vanilla baseline matches skill/memory modules; argues run-to-run variance is a core metric; template for budget-matched comparison and our noise floor.

title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
relation_to_ours: Fixed-cost-level comparison with inference vs tool spend split; analogous to our cached vs uncached split.

title: BAGEN: Are LLM Agents Budget-Aware?
relation_to_ours: Budget as a control signal; early stopping saves 28-64% tokens on failures; tangential to layout.

title: LongFuncEval: Measuring the effectiveness of long context models for function calling
relation_to_ours: Accuracy drops 7-85% with catalog size, 7-91% with response length, 13-40% with conversation length; why the tool block is fixed and why length is a factor in our design.

title: RAG-MCP: Mitigating Prompt Bloat in LLM Tool Selection via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
relation_to_ours: Dynamic tool retrieval: tokens -50%+, selection accuracy 13.62% to 43.13%; load-on-demand breaks the tool prefix and is never priced; mask-vs-remove still unmeasured.

title: Dynamic ReAct: Scalable Tool Selection for Large-Scale MCP Environments
relation_to_ours: Search-and-load tool selection, up to 50% less tool loading at maintained accuracy; cache-hostile by construction.

title: Semantic Tool Discovery for Large Language Models: A Vector-Based Approach to MCP Tool Selection
relation_to_ours: Embedding-based MCP tool retrieval; practitioner trend toward dynamic tool loading; no caching.

title: How Many Tools Should an LLM Agent See? A Chance-Corrected Answer
relation_to_ours: Shortlist-depth metric; Claude Sonnet 4.6 selection 93.1% adaptive vs 87.1% fixed-5; quantifies tool-count effect, supports a small fixed tool set as control.

title: Try, Check and Retry: A Divide-and-Conquer Framework for Boosting Long-context Tool-Calling Performance of LLMs
relation_to_ours: Accuracy falls for every model as candidate tools grow on BFCL (our T2 benchmark); Tool-DC +25.1%.

title: Toolshed: Scale Tool-Equipped Agents with Advanced RAG-Tool Fusion and Tool Knowledge Bases
relation_to_ours: Varies tool count and top-k against agent performance and token cost; earliest explicit accuracy-vs-tool-count-vs-cost study here.

title: OSWorld-MCP: Benchmarking MCP Tool Invocation In Computer-Use Agents
relation_to_ours: 158-tool computer-use benchmark; marginal; schema volume as context cost.

title: You Need an Encoder for Native Position-Independent Caching
relation_to_ours: States existing PIC methods incur substantial accuracy loss; trained encoder (COMB) recovers it; confirms non-prefix reuse is not free, motivating study of the API-level prefix discipline.

title: KVBoost: Chunk-Level Key-Value Cache Reuse with Deviation-Guided Recomputation for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
relation_to_ours: Chunk reuse with boundary recompute holds 99.2% vs 99.1% accuracy at 4.49x lower TTFT; L2 is the no-recompute, full-price version of moving content.

title: C$^2$KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference
relation_to_ours: Naive compression plus non-prefix reuse causes severe accuracy degradation; learned composable KV; same message from the storage side.
